subject: Prod hosting options for MindWell regulated pilot
messages:
From: Laurel Miller <laurel.miller@mindwellhealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: MindWell Procurement <procurement@mindwellhealth.com>, mtech@mindwellhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Prod hosting options for MindWell regulated pilot

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo today — the team was impressed by the latency profile and the observability in Redwood Console. We have a narrow window to stand up a pilot for our EU-regulated line of business (PHI in scope). Key non-negotiables: EU data residency, SOC 2 evidence, customer-level audit logs, ability to isolate workload (no multi-tenant co-tenancy with other customers), and a p95 latency target under 200ms for short-form generation.

Traffic profile for pilot: peak ~80 requests/sec, avg prompt ~750 tokens, avg generation ~150 tokens, heavy concurrency (many short calls). Retention/backup requirements: 90 days of request logs, keys via our KMS. Procurement is asking for a clear comparison: Private (VPC/on-prem style control plane) vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) with cost/lead time/SLA tradeoffs and recommended GPU fleet sizing. Can you provide a short written comparison + ballpark ARR impact and any required procurement steps? We also attached a short requirements spreadsheet.

Procurement timeline: decision by May 7 if possible.

Best,
Laurel
Dr. Laurel Miller
Head of Applied AI, MindWell Health
laurel.miller@mindwellhealth.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Prod hosting options for MindWell regulated pilot

Hi Laurel — thanks for the clear requirements and the sheet. I'm looping in Karthik (infra sizing) and Marissa (commercial/legal). Below is a concise comparison and a proposed next step: a 30-minute call to review numbers and confirm telemetry/retention detail.

Short comparison (high level):
- Private deployment (VPC/private control plane or on-prem):
  * Pros: Maximum isolation, easiest path for EU residency + KMS/HSM integration, full audit log control. Simplifies some compliance asks.
  * Cons: Longer lead time (2–6 weeks for customer-managed networking & onboarding), higher fixed infra ops & minimum GPU footprint. Typically higher initial cost.
  * Rough sizing for your pilot (see Karthik's calc): 6x H100 or 8x A100-class equivalents for consistent p95 <200ms at 80 rps with requested token sizes if using quantized models and our KV cache.

- Dedicated (Redwood reserved capacity):
  * Pros: Fast ramp (days), predictable monthly commit, built-in autoscale/burst options, lower immediate TCO for short pilots. Maintains Redwood control plane for faster ops.
  * Cons: Needs strict tenancy isolation guarantees (we offer isolated fleets per customer) and contractual SLA/terms for audit data access. Slightly less control vs customer-managed private network.
  * Rough sizing: 10x A100-equivalent GPUs in eu-west region (committed pool) with burst buffer for peak demand; can start with 6 GPUs plus burst (cost + scaling tradeoff).

Recommended next step: Karthik to validate numerics and attach a capacity file. Marissa will propose a procurement pathway (12-month commit + onboarding SLAs). I attached a commercial outline and our SOC2 summary for review.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Prod hosting options for MindWell regulated pilot

Vivek / Laurel — quick note on the numbers and assumptions I used (see attached CSV):
Assumptions:
- Model footprint: 30B parameter family, Q8 quantization for A100/H100 kernels.
- Service pattern: 80 rps peak, 750-in / 150-out tokens, average 900 tokens per request processed end-to-end.
- Latency target: p95 <200ms (including network + decode).

Sizing summary (pilot):
- Private (customer-managed VPC): 6x H100 (or 8x A100-80GB equiv) configured for low-latency inference with 1.5x reserved concurrency headroom. This assumes no token-level batching beyond our continuous batching; KV cache for prefix reuse reduces effective compute by ~25% for repeat prompts.
- Dedicated (Redwood reserved pool): Option A (conservative): 10x A100 equiv with autoscale config and 2x burst nodes for traffic spikes. Option B (cost-optimized): Start with 6x A100 equiv + burst to 10 for peaks; require an autoscale-policy with burst credits.

Cost delta (rough monthly run-rate, eu-west, list-price proxies):
- Private: CAPEX-equivalent ramp + onboarding professional services — ballpark USD 85k–120k/month equiv (includes HSM/KMS integration and private networking ops amortized).
- Dedicated: Monthly commit ~USD 45k–70k depending on commit length and discount. 12-month commit reduces unit cost ~20%.

Operational notes:
- For Private we recommend on Day 1 a minimal observability export (90-day logs to S3 with access controls) and a 30-day warm-up window for KV cache population.
- For Dedicated we can provide the same audit logs and KMS integrations but will require an SLA addendum for data egress and dedicated fleet isolation.

I'll attach capacity_run_estimates.csv with per-GPU latency curves and a short runbook for warm-up. If the customer wants a blended approach, we can do Dedicated for initial pilot with an option to migrate to Private ahead of full production.

-Karthik
Lead Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
--- attachment: capacity_run_estimates.csv ---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-30T13:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Prod hosting options for MindWell regulated pilot

Circling on procurement/commercial asks from Procurement side. A few pragmatic items: 
- We can offer Dedicated with isolated fleet + EU residency controls under a 12-month commit. For Private we treat that as an enterprise package (platform fee + support).
- Onboarding credit: propose 10% credit applied to first invoice if MindWell signs 12-month commit within 30 days. This helps mitigate migration risk.
- SLA: standard Redwood SLA applies for Dedicated. For Private we'll add an SLA appendix showing uptime and RTO for control plane issues; lead time to negotiate is ~2 weeks.
- Data & audit access: we can deliver 90-day logs and per-token tracing; for Private we can deliver raw access to the S3 bucket under customer KMS. For Dedicated we'll expose logs via secure link and HMACed daily exports.

Procurement steps I recommend we capture in a mutual action plan doc: 1) Technical sign-off (7 days), 2) Legal SOW & PO (7–14 days), 3) Onboarding & infra build (7–21 days depending on Private vs Dedicated).

I'll draft the MAP doc and circulate; for now, if MindWell is timeline-constrained I recommend starting Dedicated (fastest) with an optional migration path to Private in Q2 post-pilot.

-Marissa
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is very helpful. Procurement likes the Dedicated-first recommendation with the optional migration path to Private; the 10% onboarding credit helps. Two quick asks before our May 7 decision:
1) Can you send a short one-page runbook for the Dedicated onboarding (networking ports, expected IPs, KMS handshake steps)?
2) Can you confirm whether the dedicated isolated fleet will produce per-customer raw logs (not just aggregated) and whether we can push those to our EU S3?

If yes to both, we should be able to sign fast. Can we book a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize details?

Best,
Laurel
